Threat.value: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place

Memory.value: When I try to deliberately remember what happened I find it difficult to access the memory
The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

vignette: Amir's eyes would scan the rooftops he worked on with a mixture of pride and wariness. A veteran roofer, he had seen his share of accidents, but nothing could have prepared him for the day he was exposed to toxic chemicals on the job site. The memory of that incident, now over a year old, still lingered in his mind like an unwelcome guest. As he worked, Amir would often find himself thinking about his grandchildren, who loved visiting their grandfather at work. Being around children usually brought him joy, but nowadays it also triggered memories of the accident. He remembered how one of his coworkers had rushed to wash off the chemicals with water, while others stood frozen in fear. The sound of sirens and the smell of disinfectant would transport Amir back to that chaotic scene, and he'd feel a wave of anxiety wash over him. Trying to recall the details of that day deliberately proved difficult for Amir. His mind seemed to recoil from the memories, as if trying to protect itself from the pain. Yet, at night, when he lay in bed, the memory would force its way into his consciousness, playing out like a gruesome movie reel. He'd wake up with a start, drenched in sweat, unable to shake off the feeling of unease that lingered long after he opened his eyes. Amir's inability to relax even in safe spaces was starting to take a toll on his relationships. His wife would try to comfort him, but he'd flinch at her touch, as if expecting another catastrophe to strike at any moment. His sleep problems had become so severe that he'd often fall asleep during the day, exhausted from the previous night's ordeal. The media coverage of similar accidents only made things worse for Amir. News stories about workers exposed to toxic chemicals would send him spiraling back into memories of his own experience. He began avoiding social gatherings and even stopped going to family events, fearing he'd run into people who might trigger another memory flashback. As the months went by, Amir became increasingly withdrawn. His wife noticed that he was spending more time alone on the rooftop during work hours, "just making sure everything is safe," as he'd say. In reality, Amir was trying to avoid any potential triggers that might set off another chain reaction of memories and anxiety. Amir's life had become a delicate balancing act between avoiding triggers and managing his own fears. It wasn't until his wife confronted him about the changes she saw in him that Amir realized he needed help. He couldn't keep living like this, constantly on edge, waiting for the other shoe to drop. With a mix of trepidation and hope, Amir made an appointment with a therapist, hoping to finally break free from the cycle of memories, threats, and triggers that had taken over his life.
